title: CSV export for the orders list
brief: A small Express app (about 2,000 lines, Jest tests via npm test) needs GET /orders.csv returning the rows GET /orders shows, with its filters, a header row and RFC 4180 quoting. The tests cover the JSON route well; there is a review checklist in docs/REVIEW-CHECKLIST.md. Nothing irreversible is involved, and the owner wants it cheap unless there is a reason not to be.

candidates.label: Lean
candidates.rationale: The route is small and the behaviour is fully checkable: the tests can assert the header, the quoting and that filters match the JSON route. When tests define done, a fast builder grinding against them is the smallest graph that works. Five rounds and thirty minutes cap the spend.
pros: cheapest and fastest: one fast agent and the test suite
the tests it writes stay behind as the regression net
cons: nobody reads the code but the builder; quoting edge cases are only as good as the tests it thinks of
no human sees the change before it lands in the branch

candidates.label: Reviewed
candidates.rationale: The project already has a review checklist, so an isolated critic has an inspectable bar and can catch what tests miss: streaming for large result sets, content-disposition, a filter the CSV route forgot. A human approves the merge. It costs a second agent per round but no planning pass.
pros: a second reader against the checklist the project already keeps
cons: builder and critic both run on the strong tier, so the critic may share the builder's blind spots (W_HOMOGENEOUS_CRITICS)
about twice the spend of Lean per round

candidates.label: Rigorous
candidates.rationale: A frontier planner writes ACCEPTANCE.md first (which filters, which encodings, what happens at ten thousand rows) and the owner approves it before any code is written; the critic then judges against that answer key. It is the right shape if 'the same rows' hides decisions nobody has made yet.
pros: the edge cases are decided and approved up front, in writing
the critic judges against an answer key made for this change
cons: the planning pass and an extra approval cost more than the change itself if the spec is already obvious

recommendation.why: The behaviour is fully testable and nothing is irreversible, so tests are the bar; pay for a critic only if you want someone to read the code.
